answer: A grove stays honest when each new identity pays a registration fee that grows with how many identities its funding wallet has already created — the first is nearly free, the tenth costs a hundred times more, the hundredth ten thousand. The fee is burned, not banked, so nobody profits from farming it. A lone lantern of a genuine newcomer slips through cheaply, while a farmer trying to spin up a thousand clones faces a cost spiral that outruns any reward the clones could harvest. The price follows the funder, not the face.
